artDirection: Industrial science-fiction Metroidvania: articulated armored/mechanical actors on hand-detailed steel modular terrain, cool structural palette against warm/cool biome-specific hazard and energy accents.
renderingStyle: 2D orthographic pixel art, manually authored articulated part geometry (native low-resolution construction, not downsampled painting); restrained 1px dark contour outline with selective pale upper-edge highlights on beveled armor planes.

lighting.direction: upper-left key light, cool and slightly diffuse
lighting.contrast: moderate — bright steel upper planes, dark blue-black joint cavities, no full-black quantization
lighting.ambient: biome-tinted ambient fill (warm amber for foundry, cool teal for flooded utility, soft green-luminous for overgrown reactor)
lighting.emissive: gameplay-meaning-only emissive accents: cyan for player/interaction, amber for boss/telegraph/hazard, never used decoratively on inert geometry

language.characters: 3-head-scale compact armored/mechanical bipeds; silhouette-first archetypes (compact, hunched-broad, tall-thin, hovering, wide-heavy) so role reads before color does.
language.environments: modular 32px steel panel kit: floor/wall/ceiling/platform/outer-corner/inner-corner/transition tiles, explicit adjacency (not auto-tiled), biome dressing changes material/wear/growth only.
language.enemies: rust/oxidized base material across all biomes (gameplay-meaning color, not biome-tinted) so an enemy silhouette is recognizable as hostile regardless of biome.
language.bosses: broad reactor/furnace-class silhouette, amber accent identical across biomes (gameplay-meaning color), scale approximately double a regular actor.
language.props: flat rounded-rectangle / cylinder geometry with a single accent stripe or window; biome dressing changes surface material and wear, not silhouette.
language.ui: flat steel-panel chrome, cyan interactive highlight, amber warning/telegraph highlight.
language.vfx: small flat polygon shapes (projectile bolts, impact bursts); amber/cyan gameplay-meaning coloring, never biome-tinted.

silhouetteRules: Every actor archetype must be identifiable in flat black silhouette alone before any color is applied.
Player silhouette stays compact and upright across all biomes and all generation variation.
Enemy archetypes (melee/ranged/flying/armored-heavy) each occupy a distinct silhouette family; no two archetypes may share a bounding proportion and equipment read.
Boss silhouette is the widest/tallest actor silhouette in its biome and carries one unambiguous weak-point read (a exposed core/vent/joint).
Terrain tiles read as flat modular panels; no tile may imply a silhouette element (character, prop) that gameplay does not place there.
materialRules: Interior material values (mid-tones) must be preserved; flattening to pure black/white silhouette is a shading-pass failure, not a stylistic choice.
Steel/armor material keeps a beveled highlight edge on its uppermost plane in every biome.
Biome material swaps (oxidation, moisture, vegetation) change surface treatment only — they never change an actor's proportions, anchor points, or gameplay-meaning accent colors.
Rivets, panel seams, and engraved joins stay visible at native resolution; they are not smoothed away by any post-process.
animationRules: Diffusion or other generated reference material may inform material and silhouette ideas only; final actor pixels are manually authored articulated part geometry, never diffusion-retained pixels.
No whole-sprite sliding, tinting, or single-still relabeling counts as an animation clip.
Attack clips require windup, extension/strike, and recovery phases at minimum.
Death clips collapse articulated body parts with a per-actor fall direction/magnitude; a shared tip-over across all actors is a defect.
Right-facing sheets are the source of truth; left-facing is a horizontal mirror, including which side equipment renders on — disclosed, not hidden.
Ground-contact frames anchor locomotion to the actor's foot pivot; floating feet during a grounded clip is a defect.
forbiddenTraits: Text, letters, watermarks, or logos baked into any sprite.
Copying the silhouette, palette, or name of an existing commercial game's iconic character or enemy.
Biome-tinting a gameplay-meaning color (player cyan, boss/hazard amber, enemy rust base) — these stay constant so players can read gameplay state independent of biome.
Pure-black or pure-white quantization of any interior material surface.
An enemy archetype silhouette that is only a recolor of another archetype's geometry.
consistencyConstraints: All character-family sprites share the same tile/pixel density and foot-pivot convention regardless of biome.

A seed may vary panel wear, growth coverage, corrosion pattern, and non-gameplay decorative detail; it may never vary an actor's anatomy proportions, its lighting direction, or a gameplay-meaning accent color.
Every biome's terrain kit exposes the same tile-role set (floor/wall/ceiling/platform/outer-corner/inner-corner/transition) so room composition logic is biome-agnostic.
Every reference image is labeled as concept/reference art and is not itself treated as a game-ready sprite sheet unless it also exists as a compiled, QA-reviewed asset in a pack manifest.
